background: Bank of China (Hong Kong) is one of the three note-issuing banks in Hong Kong and the second-largest there, a subsidiary of Bank of China, funded by Hong Kong deposits and lending to local corporates, households and across Southeast Asia.
synthesis: Rated A+ on average across all three, all three on a stable outlook, after a one-notch upgrade by one of the three on 14 Nov 2024. The balance sheet is strong against Asian banks on every measure, with CET1 of 23.8%, LCR of 168% and NSFR of 144% all in the top quarter. The one move to note is LCR, down 17 points since 30 Jun 2025, still well above the peer median. No rating action has been taken in the last 90 days.
